81434.subject: Keystone Will Destroy 18,835 Wallets After Key Theft
81434.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Anthropic](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/anthropic-files-for-ipo-with-16-3-billion-in-first-half-revenue)**[ filed for its IPO; perps imply ~$1.9T](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/anthropic-files-for-ipo-with-16-3-billion-in-first-half-revenue)

* **[Keystone](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/keystone-to-destroy-18-835-wallets-after-device-authentication-key-theft)**[ will destroy 18,835 wallets after key theft](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/keystone-to-destroy-18-835-wallets-after-device-authentication-key-theft)

* **[X100](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/x100-exploit-nets-4-85-million-usdt-after-governance-takeover)**[ lost $4.85M to a governance takeover](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/x100-exploit-nets-4-85-million-usdt-after-governance-takeover)

* **[Hyperliquid](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/hyperliquid-tests-permissioned-markets-for-payward-s-us-perps-plan)**[ tests permissioned markets for US perps](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/hyperliquid-tests-permissioned-markets-for-payward-s-us-perps-plan)

* **[Chainlink](https://thedefiant.io/converge/defi/chainlink-introduces-custodysync-with-anchorage-for-custodied-defi-borrowing)**[ lets custodied assets back DeFi loans](https://thedefiant.io/converge/defi/chainlink-introduces-custodysync-with-anchorage-for-custodied-defi-borrowing)

Keystone is about to destroy 18,835 new hardware wallets. The company said today that an attacker [stole the key it uses to prove its wallets are genuine](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/keystone-to-destroy-18-835-wallets-after-device-authentication-key-theft). That key is written into each device at the factory and cannot be replaced, so every unsold unit that carries it has to go. Keystone has paused website shipments until it builds devices with a new key.

Keystone says the key plays no part in recovery phrases or transaction signing, and owners of genuine devices do not need to move funds.

It is the second maker's check to fail this month. Ledger's Genuine Check [passed wallets that carried spy implants](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/ledger-says-cryptobilis-sold-wallet-implants-transmit-recovery-phrases-over-lte), because it verifies only the secure chip. On Oct. 12 we wrote that a buyer can confirm the chip but cannot confirm the hardware. Our first advice was to buy direct from the maker. Keystone's breach reaches people who did just that.

Scammers also know whom to target: breaches at [Keystone](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/keystone-website-breach-exposes-customer-addresses-and-order-details), [SafePal](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/safepal-breach-exposes-39-798-customers-stolen-records-for-sale) and [Trezor's shipping provider](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/trezor-shipping-provider-breach-exposes-data-of-13-689-customers) have exposed about 146,000 customer records since August. # Investors never see everything 

In the classic Star Trek episode "The Menagerie," the _USS Enterprise_ visits a planet where a dying race of subterranean telepaths — the Talosians — endure their grim living conditions by conjuring, through sheer force of will, an alternative reality to live in.

Apple engineer Bud Tribble believed Steve Jobs had a similar power: “In his presence, reality is malleable,” Tribble [said](https://www.amazon.com/Steve-Jobs-Walter-Isaacson/dp/1982176865/ref=sr_1_1_sspa?crid=1BLU0J72Y9KLU&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.k_xqKlDXQ2Nf4zaCq1rU5M9MZgWPuKYTGtIujNDWhY3Me52PW6OZi8w8_rRYwYE31DHx0QC2PGoZstTuhAe6ZLYXD_5ZBg4u47BY7edF5aw0LN_q2ohr6qhEi1PBLPEgrpHxIkg88zWzXKrO6t84l91z9a9yR5BpOb89o75KflNth7HPJsZ-HhZAeN6i5_QgWIPJ_G1X9R8S3nG_og18IF3dGvqYshCvLGO_XxFEl84.0Jbsz5D4MUowTAtKk9wkhY4_8bUzJ2nKCvc8Rex9ENM&dib_tag=se&keywords=steve+jobs&qid=1793025362&sprefix=steve+jobs%2Caps%2C251&sr=8-1-spons&sp_csd=d2lkZ2V0TmFtZT1zcF9hdGY&psc=1). “He can convince anyone of practically anything.”

Through a Talosian-like force of will, Jobs would convince both himself and his employees that every impossible engineering request he made was, in fact, possible. Engineers who entered a meeting 100 percent sure that building the first Macintosh in less than a year was nothing but a fantasy would leave having promised to do it.

“The best way to describe the situation is a term from Star Trek,” Tribble explained. “Steve has a reality distortion field.”

Investors sometimes got caught in the field as well.
